proposals.before: Taizu took the throne when the Yaolian yuyue yielded power.
proposals.after: Taizu, as yuyue of the Yaolian clan, received the abdication.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以遙輦氏於越受禪 means Taizu received the abdication in his capacity as Yaolian yuyue, not that another Yaolian yuyue yielded to him.

proposals.before: Taizu received the abdication from the Yaolian yuyue.
proposals.after: Taizu, as the Yaolian clan's yuyue, received the abdication.
proposals.reason: 以 marks the capacity in which Taizu received the abdication (as Yaolian yuyue), not the person from whom he received it.

proposals.before: The empress dowager, senior consort, and empress each had account-registered bureaus.
proposals.after: The empress dowager and senior consort accounts each had account-registered bureaus.
proposals.reason: Chinese only names 皇太后 and 皇太妃 accounts; the English invents an empress account not present in the source.

proposals.before: The Empress Dowager's account, the Senior Imperial Consort's account, and the Empress's account each had account-registered bureaus.
proposals.after: The Empress Dowager's account and the Senior Imperial Consort's account each had account-registered bureaus.
proposals.reason: Source lists only two accounts (皇太后、皇太妃帳); Empress account is an invention.

proposals.before: Suzu's eldest Zhi Yan's line sat in the Five Courts Office; uncle Ge La, younger brother Zhi Li, and Yi's second son Tie La and younger brother Gu Zhi in the Six Courts Office.
proposals.after: Suzu's eldest son Zhi Yan's line sat in the Five Courts Office; third son Ge La, youngest son Zhi Li, and Yi Zu's second son Tie La and youngest son Gu Zhi were in the Six Courts Office.
proposals.reason: 叔子/季子 are birth-order terms for Suzu's and Yi Zu's sons, not 'uncle' or 'younger brother' relative to another sibling referent.

proposals.before: The eldest son Zhi Yan's line of Ancestor Suzu was in the Five Courts Office; uncle Ge La, younger brother Zhi Li, and Ancestor Yi's second son Tie La and younger brother Gu Zhi were all in the Six Courts Office.
proposals.after: The eldest son Zhi Yan's line of Ancestor Suzu was in the Five Courts Office; third son Ge La, youngest son Zhi Li, and Ancestor Yi's second son Tie La and youngest son Gu Zhi were all in the Six Courts Office.
proposals.reason: 叔子 and 季子 mark sons' birth order under Suzu/Yi Zu, not uncle/younger-brother relations.

proposals.before: Xuanzu's elder brother Malu left no heirs; second son Yan Mu's line is the Senior Father's House;
proposals.after: Xuanzu's eldest son Malu left no heirs; second son Yan Mu's line is the Senior Father's House;
proposals.reason: 伯子 means Xuanzu's eldest son, not his elder brother; parallel 次子 confirms sons of Xuanzu.

proposals.before: Ancestor Xuanzu's elder brother Malu had no heirs; the second son Yan Mu's descendants are the Senior Father's House;
proposals.after: Ancestor Xuanzu's eldest son Malu had no heirs; the second son Yan Mu's descendants are the Senior Father's House;
proposals.reason: 伯子 is eldest son of Xuanzu, parallel to 次子; 'elder brother' reverses the genealogy.

proposals.before: Uncle Shi Lu formed the Middle Father's House;
proposals.after: The third son Shi Lu formed the Middle Father's House;
proposals.reason: 叔子 continues Xuanzu's sons by birth order (after 伯子/次子), not an uncle of Xuanzu.

proposals.before: Uncle Shi Lu is called the Middle Father's House;
proposals.after: The third son Shi Lu is called the Middle Father's House;
proposals.reason: 叔子 is Xuanzu's third son in the same genealogical sequence, not 'uncle'.
提轄 is the office name tixia; “tirua” is a corrupted transliteration not supported by the Chinese.

proposals.before: Senior Imperial Consort Xiaowen Dunmu Palace and Wenzhong Princely Establishment
proposals.after: Xiaowen Imperial Younger Brother Dunmu Palace and Wenzhong Princely Establishment
proposals.reason: 皇太弟 means imperial younger brother (heir as the emperor’s younger brother), not “Senior Imperial Consort.”

proposals.before: Senior Imperial Consort Xiaowen Dunmu Palace; Wenzhong Princely Establishment
proposals.after: Xiaowen Imperial Younger Brother Dunmu Palace; Wenzhong Princely Establishment
proposals.reason: 皇太弟 means imperial younger brother, not “Senior Imperial Consort”; the literal field repeats the same error.

decisions.reason: In s0085, 以遙輦氏於越受禪 marks the capacity in which Taizu received abdication (as Yaolian yuyue), matching the Great Yuyue Office context; the idiomatic wrongly treats a separate Yaolian yuyue as the one who yielded.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太祖以遙輦氏於越受禪

decisions.reason: The same 以…受禪 construction in s0085 means Taizu received abdication as the Yaolian clan's yuyue; reading 遙輦氏於越 as the giver is a misparse of 以.
s0165 names only 皇太后、皇太妃帳; the idiomatic invents a third empress account not in the Chinese.
The literal likewise adds an Empress's account; the source lists only the Empress Dowager's and Senior Imperial Consort's accounts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皇太后、皇太妃帳，皆有著帳諸局

decisions.reason: In s0186, 叔子 and 季子 are birth-order labels for Suzu's and Yi Zu's sons (parallel to 長子/仲子), not 'uncle' or 'younger brother'; the proposed kinship terms restore that sequence and name 懿祖 as Yi Zu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 肅祖長子…叔子葛剌、季子洽禮及懿祖仲子帖剌、季子古直

decisions.reason: The literal of s0186 makes the same kinship error; third son / youngest son correctly render 叔子 and 季子 under Suzu and Yi Zu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 叔子葛剌、季子洽禮及懿祖仲子帖剌、季子古直

decisions.reason: 玄祖伯子麻鲁 pairs with 次子岩木 in s0188; 伯子 is Xuanzu's eldest son, so 'elder brother' reverses the genealogy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 玄祖伯子麻鲁无后，次子岩木

decisions.reason: The literal likewise misreads 伯子 as elder brother; eldest son matches the birth-order series continued by 次子、叔子、季子.
s0189 叔子釋魯 continues Xuanzu's sons after 伯子/次子 in s0188; 'uncle' invents a wrong kinship link.
The literal of s0189 makes the same error; third son correctly renders 叔子 in this genealogical sequence.
s0297 is 某宮提轄司; 提轄 romanizes as tixia, and tirua is an unsupported corruption.
孝文皇太弟 is Xiaowen Imperial Younger Brother (皇太弟), not Senior Imperial Consort (皇太妃); the proposed title matches the Chinese.
The literal of s0315 repeats the same 皇太弟→Senior Imperial Consort error; Xiaowen Imperial Younger Brother restores the correct title.
